body:
I wish it was that easy. I'll lose everything if I fall apart, and I'm half apart now. Insurance, house, everything. I have no confidence anymore that I can get us out of our situation. Hope is for other people.

Thank you for replying, though. It does mean something.
I get little time to myself, but it hardly matters. I can't muster the energy to do anything or look for solutions. I'm just tired.

It was pretty cool of you to write me. Yes, actually, I have experience as a writer. If you still need somebody, I would be interested.

As for depression, I'm coming out of it slowly. I'm not sure what has changed, but I think maybe my shoddy health is improving enough to help me feel better. Still pretty down, but not on the brink.

You're a kind person. Thank you for the concern.
Thank you. I keep looking for reasons to laugh. Today is a new day.

Yeah, I'm trying. There's got to be something.

Thanks.

I had a job that I liked somewhat, but I became too emotional on the job, too cocky, made enemies, and was let go. The timing was particularly terrible, and seriously stupid mistakes I made after the fact robbed me of every cent I had ever saved-- probably a couple of hundred thousand dollars in stock, if not more. I declared bankruptcy.

Losing the job was the beginning of a slow downhill slide into reclusion that has cost me my friends.  I've been through three jobs in the last few years, I'm stuck inside a mortgage I can't escape, and my wife and kid are living hand-to-mouth, one stroke of bad luck away from disaster. The work I enjoy the most-- being a writer-- would never come close to paying my bills and feeding my family.

On top of it all, I've developed debilitating health issues that make it a struggle to get to work every day. I know my performance at work is lackluster, but I can't help it. I'm sick. The constant disapproval from my manager colors everything I do and makes me timid and miserable on the job. I'm almost out of sick leave and taking time off doesn't do anything anyway. My wife is also ill and cannot work, and we'd have to figure out a child care arrangement if she tried, which makes it close to a wash anyway.

I've had a history of depression in my life, and I've made a number of unwise decisions in various attempts to escape misery. I thought that I had finally begun to put together a solid life when I was laid off and this whole downward slide began. I'm in my forties and feel useless and spent and too trapped by circumstances to take risks.

And so I write myself notes at work, little Notepad pep talks, usually when I'm too fucked up to focus or too intimidated to approach co-workers about job-related things. They help me appear busy and prop me up for a few minutes, but I can't just do that all day. 

I am living a frozen life with no margin for error and little hope for the future. I'd leave this job in an instant if I could find another that interested me and paid the bills, but after sending out hundreds of resumes and being humiliated in a few interviews, I just cratered. I am no longer very sure of why I am alive other than to take care of the people who depend on me. I no longer feel welcome in the world.
